project.name: GPAC
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source reviewed here is the prepared checkout at `9ed3d8d5cedca53d3c2933f3c64b4737202ba713` (`add bsdbg option in av1 reframer`). It is neither descended from the metadata `reported_vulnerable_commit` nor from the metadata `fixed_commit`, but the staged `patch.diff` still targets the same vulnerable `gf_isom_box_array_read_ex()` size-check block present in this checkout, and the saved ASan trace line map matches this exact source (`gf_isom_box_del:1778`, `audio_sample_entry_box_read:3966`, `gf_isom_delete_movie:935`).

classification.classification_note: The issue description and fix are framed as missing invalid-file rejection for an oversized child box, but the reproduced manifestation is a heap-use-after-free READ during cleanup because the oversized child stays registered, is later freed through the wrong parent list, and is then traversed again from the original owner list.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42494822 (gpac): Heap-use-after-free READ 8 found by fuzz target fuzz_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42494822
bug_description.normalized: The staged 159-byte witness is parsed as a root `mp4a` sample-entry box whose payload contains a `wave` child declared as 32 bytes and an `esds` sub-box declared as 115 bytes. Before `wave` children are read, `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` converts that 32-byte declaration into a 24-byte payload remainder (`newBox->size = size - hdr_size`). In vulnerable `gf_isom_box_array_read_ex()`, the `wave` parser then observes `0x18 < 0x73` but only logs the problem and sets `parent->size = 0`; it still registers the oversized `esds` in `wave->child_boxes`. Returning from `wave`, `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` detects that 123 bytes were consumed for a 32-byte box, seeks back to the declared end of `wave`, and the outer `mp4a` parser re-enters `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` on mid-`esds` bytes, producing the nonzero status that sends `audio_sample_entry_box_read()` into its fallback `esds` scan. The concrete `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` case in `audio_sample_entry_on_child_box()` has already aliased that inner `esds` as `ptr->esd` without moving it out of `wave->child_boxes`. The fallback scan then calls `gf_isom_box_del_parent(&ptr->child_boxes, ptr->esd)` through the outer mp4a list instead of the `wave` child list, freeing the `esds` object without unlinking it from `wave->child_boxes`. When `gf_isom_open_file()` later tears the partially parsed tree down on error, generic box deletion walks `wave->child_boxes` and reuses that dangling pointer; `gf_isom_box_del()` then reads from the freed `esds` object and AddressSanitizer reports a heap-use-after-free READ at `src/isomedia/box_funcs.c:1778`.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes the attacker-controlled byte stream and materializes ISO BMFF box size/type words. On the witness path this header parser first admits the root `mp4a` box and later materializes the forged `wave` and `esds` headers that drive the bug.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is 159 bytes (sha256 `5d6fa7b708d9d7289aea3644a19d40addad6d119435a6ee8a21afacdbb16f73f`). Its first 8 bytes are `00 00 00 00 6d 70 34 61`, so the root header is parsed as `size = 0`, `type = 'mp4a'`. The vulnerability-relevant child headers later consumed by this same statement are `00 00 00 20 77 61 76 65` at offset `0x24` (`wave`, size `0x20`) and `00 00 00 73 65 73 64 73` at offset `0x2c` (`esds`, size `0x73`).

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The forged box extents originate here. The witness's `wave` header yields declared `size = 0x20`, which `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` later turns into a 24-byte payload remainder (`newBox->size = 0x18`) before nested parsing; the nested `esds` header yields `size = 0x73`. Those attacker-controlled values reach the oversized-child predicate as `parent->size = 0x18` and `a->size = 0x73`.

root_cause.description: When a parsed child box is larger than the current container payload remainder, vulnerable code only logs and zeroes the remaining container size. It does not destroy the oversized child and does not return `GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE`, so the malformed child survives into the parent's ownership lists.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `gf_isom_box_del(a); return GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE;` at this exact site (guarded by `!gf_opts_get_bool("core", "no-check")`), which prevents the oversized child from ever being registered.

sink.description: ASan crash site. Generic box destruction reuses a freed `GF_ESDBox *` from `wave->child_boxes` and reads the first box fields from released heap memory.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `READ of size 8` at `src/isomedia/box_funcs.c:1778:19`, 24 bytes inside the 48-byte `esds` allocation that was already freed from `audio_sample_entry_box_read()`.

parser_admitted.description: The root `mp4a` header has already dispatched into the audio sample-entry parser, so the witness is now inside the vulnerable child-box parsing and fallback-recovery logic.

fine_trace.note: The first 8 witness bytes are consumed here as `size = 0`, `type = GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_MP4A`. Because zero-sized boxes are allowed only at root and expand to the remaining file size, this dispatches the entire 159-byte blob into `audio_sample_entry_box_read()` as a root `mp4a` sample entry.
Once inside `mp4a` child parsing, the same header parser reads the bytes at offset `0x24` as `size = 0x20`, `type = GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE`, materializing a `wave` box declared as 32 bytes.

Before `wave` children are read, `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` converts the declared 32-byte `wave` box into a 24-byte payload remainder by subtracting the 8-byte header. This `0x18` remainder becomes the `parent->size` used by nested `wave` parsing.
Inside `def_parent_box_read()` for that `wave`, the nested header at offset `0x2c` is parsed as `size = 0x73`, `type = GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_ESDS`, so the child claims 115 bytes.

Root cause. The `wave` reader compares the 24-byte payload remainder from step 3 against the nested `esds` size from step 4 and observes `0x18 < 0x73`, but it only logs the mismatch and zeroes `parent->size`. The malformed `esds` object stays alive instead of being deleted and rejected.
Control falls through from step 5 into the always-register block, so the oversized `esds` is linked into `wave->child_boxes` as if it were a valid child.

The executed callback is the concrete `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` case. Because `s->type == GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_MP4A`, it binds `cfg_ptr` to `&ptr->esd`, scans `wave->child_boxes`, and stores the inner `esds` from step 6 into `*cfg_ptr`, so `ptr->esd` aliases that same object. No ownership transfer runs on the crashing path, because the later sink still traverses `wave->child_boxes`.

Returning from `def_parent_box_read()`, GPAC notices that the `wave` parser consumed 123 bytes even though the `wave` header declared only 32. It logs the invalid read and seeks back to `start+size = 0x44`, so outer `mp4a` child parsing resumes at the declared end of `wave` while most of the oversized `esds` bytes still remain in the payload.

The outer `mp4a` child loop re-enters `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` at offset `0x44`, now in the middle of the original `esds` payload. The bytes `20 20 ff 20 20 20 ff 20` are reinterpreted as a bogus header with `size = 0x2020ff20` and `type = 0x2020ff20`.

Only 83 bytes remain after the bogus header from step 9, so the claimed payload size `0x2020ff18` is impossible. `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` therefore returns `GF_ISOM_INCOMPLETE_FILE` and hands the partially created box back through `*outBox`.

The resumed outer-child parse turns the malformed-header failure from step 10 into its own nonzero return value: it deletes the partial box from step 10 and returns `e` to `audio_sample_entry_box_read()`. This is the source-level error edge that makes the later `if (!e)` test fail.

Because step 11 made `e` nonzero, `audio_sample_entry_box_read()` bypasses its normal success return and falls into the fallback `esds` bytescan. That recovery path finds `esds` bytes in the original sample-entry payload and calls `gf_isom_box_del_parent(&ptr->child_boxes, ptr->esd)` on the aliased inner box from step 7.

Here `child_boxes` is `&ptr->child_boxes`, whose entries are outer `mp4a` children such as the `wave` box. `gf_list_del_item()` therefore does not unlink the inner `esds` object, and the stale pointer remains stored in `wave->child_boxes` from step 6.

The same helper immediately frees the `esds` object. In the saved free stack this descends into `gf_isom_box_del() -> esds_box_del() -> gf_free()`, so `wave->child_boxes` now contains a dangling `GF_ESDBox *`.

The saved crash stack reaches `gf_isom_delete_movie()` from `gf_isom_open_file()` line 882, which witnesses that open still ends on this `mov->LastError` cleanup path after the recovery work above. That teardown recursively destroys the partially built `mp4a` tree, including `wave->child_boxes`.

During that teardown, `gf_isom_box_array_reset()` iterates the still-populated `wave->child_boxes`, retrieves the dangling `esds` pointer, and passes it back into `gf_isom_box_del()` as if it were still live.

ASan sink. `a` is the freed `esds` pointer from step 16, so this field read dereferences released heap memory. The saved trace reports `READ of size 8` here, 24 bytes inside the 48-byte `esds` allocation freed in step 14.

format.name: GPAC ISO BMFF / QuickTime-style audio sample entry blob
format.contract: Use the exact staged 159-byte `poc` (sha256 `5d6fa7b708d9d7289aea3644a19d40addad6d119435a6ee8a21afacdbb16f73f`). Its witness semantics are: root header `00 00 00 00 6d 70 34 61` (`size = 0`, `type = 'mp4a'`); then, at offset `0x24`, `00 00 00 20 77 61 76 65` (`wave`, declared size `0x20`, which GPAC reduces to a 24-byte payload remainder before nested parsing); then, at offset `0x2c`, `00 00 00 73 65 73 64 73` (`esds`, declared size `0x73`). After `wave` overreads that child, GPAC seeks back to offset `0x44` and reinterprets the mid-`esds` bytes there as a new header. That exact layout makes GPAC keep the inner `esds` in `wave->child_boxes`, free it during fallback `esds` recovery in `audio_sample_entry_box_read()`, and later reuse the dangling pointer during generic box destruction. The trigger semantics recorded here do not generalize beyond this exact witness layout.
